params.body:
On the sign-in page, Chrome on Android offers a saved login only when the password field is tapped, not the email field. The email field is marked `autocomplete="email"`, which a password manager reads as a contact address and not as the account name of a login. A sign-in form's identifier is `autocomplete="username"`, also when it is an email address.

## What changes

- `autocomplete="username"` on the address field of the three forms that pair it with a password: sign in, register and reset password. Register and reset password then save the new login under the address as well.
- Forgot password has no password field and keeps `autocomplete="email"`.
- The fields stay `type="email"`, so the phone still shows the email keyboard.

## Checked

- `PasswordResetTest::test_the_address_is_the_username_wherever_a_password_goes_with_it`: sign in and register mark the address as username. It fails without the change.
- Full suite 555/556. `BuildStampTest` fails in any worktree because the branch ref lives in the common git dir.
- Pint passes.
params.title: Mark the sign-in address as the username, so Android offers saved logins from it
